clue.text: One serving American wearing very large watch

indicators.note: whatever is wearing something has it on the outside, so the outer letters wrap around the inner ones

blocks.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very
the Roman numeral for one
a GI is an American soldier
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A US soldier is sporting an enormous wristwatch.
explanation.walkthrough: One and the serving American join as IGI, which sits inside very-plus-large, V...L, giving VIGIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a period of keeping watch, especially through the night, so the noun swaps cleanly.

clue.text: Surprisingly civil about small group being malicious

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly is not as expected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order
about means surrounding, so the shuffled word wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to rearrange
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: Unexpectedly, a polite little band turns out to be spiteful.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriolic speech is bitter and venomous, full of ill will.

clue.text: Train chess whiz to take piece (not king)

indicators.note: not king means the letter that stands for king is left out
to take something in is to hold it, so one word is placed inside another

blocks.note: GM is a grandmaster
a rook is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A grandmaster captures a piece other than the king.
explanation.walkthrough: K is king in chess notation, so ROOK becomes ROO.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom someone is to prepare or train them for a role.

clue.text: Country stars purchasing lush hotel

indicators.note: purchasing means acquiring, so the outer word takes the others into itself

blocks.note: Leo is a constellation, a group of stars
a lush and a sot are both drunkards
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Celebrities are buying a luxurious hotel abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lush' looks like an adjective for the hotel but is a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small mountain kingdom surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Perhaps Poet Laureate admitting nothing's right

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it inside, so the outer word takes the other in

blocks.note: a Poet Laureate might be called a star bard, a leading poet; 'Perhaps' marks it as an example
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The nation's official poet confesses that nothing is going well.
explanation.walkthrough: STAR BARD takes O just after the B to make STARBOARD; the apostrophe-s is 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the nautical term for the right-hand side of a ship when facing forward.

clue.text: Break down after ashes finally scattered

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of ashes
to parse a sentence is to break it down into its parts

explanation.surface: Someone collapses after a loved one's ashes have been strewn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the analysis word behind the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly spread, scattered rather than dense.

clue.text: Two mammals conserving last of warmth in the furthest point from the sun

definitions.text: the furthest point from the sun

indicators.note: last of picks out the closing letter of the next word
conserving means keeping safe within, so one animal holds the letter inside

blocks.note: first mammal: an ape
the final letter of warmth
second mammal: a lion; 'Two' says there are two animals

explanation.surface: A pair of animals keeping warm even at the coldest, remotest point of an orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' is not a number to use: it tells you to find two separate mammals, the first of which holds the extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphelion is the astronomical term for the point in an orbit most distant from the sun.

clue.text: Jockey wore bra, causing conflict

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre and jostle, so the letters are pushed into new positions

blocks.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A racing rider in lingerie stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boer War (1899-1902) was fought between Britain and the Boer republics of southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boer War was an armed conflict, a specific war.

clue.text: A Co-operative store plugs sweetener

indicators.note: something that plugs a gap fills the middle, so it goes inside the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
SPAR is a chain of convenience stores
a tame animal is docile and co-operative

explanation.surface: A Co-op supermarket stocks an artificial sugar substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Co-operative store' reads as the Co-op chain, but it splits three ways; SPAR is a chain of convenience shops, and the store goes inside the other two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspartame is an artificial low-calorie sugar substitute.

clue.text: Saw old man penning note

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: one's old man is one's father
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone's father was seen writing a short letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a cutting tool or a proverb; it is the past tense of seeing someone romantically.
explanation.definitionFit: If you saw someone, in the sense of going out with them, you dated them.

clue.text: Leader's philosophical way is spread without resistance

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the word for spread

blocks.note: the Tao is 'the Way' of Chinese philosophy
taken as written
to spread or extend is to reach
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A leader's philosophy of life is broadcast without any opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: REACH loses its R to leave EACH. The Taoiseach is the prime minister of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taoiseach is the head of the Irish government, a national leader.

clue.text: Someone far from home once a year getting tense

blocks.note: ex means former, once
p.a. is per annum, a year
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An emigrant finds that each year away makes them more anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat (expatriate) lives outside their native country, far from home.

clue.text: Big-name actress occasionally detained people

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A famous film star has sometimes been locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Inmates are prisoners, people held in custody.

clue.text: Some buffalo were duly put down

indicators.note: some signals only a portion of the following words is taken

blocks.note: runs across the end of buffalo, all of were, and the start of duly

explanation.surface: Several bison were properly euthanised.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower something is to put it down; both are past participles here.

clue.text: Water that is cut off from US city by idiot

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
a goon is a fool

explanation.surface: Water supply to an American city is severed by some fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means beside, placing the idiot after the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of water separated from the sea by a reef or sandbank.

clue.text: Retired ordinary seaman invested in innovative green electricity producer

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the letters run backwards
innovative means new and different, so the word is remade in fresh order
money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: O is an abbreviation for ordinary
a tar is a sailor
taken as written, letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A former sailor puts money into new eco-friendly power generation.
explanation.definitionFit: A generator is a machine that produces electrical power.

clue.text: Post that supports large family over housing predicament

indicators.note: over suggests turning something round, so the family word reads backwards
housing means giving a home to, so one word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: a brood is a big family of children
being in a jam is being in a predicament

explanation.surface: A support beam is holding up a big household in a tricky situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorjamb is the upright post at the side of a door frame, carrying its weight.

clue.text: Desperately try one cab rank

indicators.note: acting desperately means frantically and wildly, so the letters fall into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A frantic traveller tries a taxi at the stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cab rank' is a taxi stand in the surface, but rank alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronetcy is the hereditary title and standing of a baronet, a British rank.

clue.text: Fired up amid argument, producing dagger

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading from the bottom, so the word runs backwards
amid means in the middle of, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: something fired is lit
a set-to is a quarrel

explanation.surface: An angry quarrel ends with someone pulling a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired up' reads as angry, but up belongs with the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slender tapering blade.

clue.text: Fleece article released by fashion firm

indicators.note: something released by a word is let go from it, so a letter drops out

blocks.note: to fleece someone is to con them
a is the indefinite article
to fashion is to create

explanation.surface: A woolly jacket is put out by a clothing company.
explanation.walkthrough: CREATE loses A to become CRETE. 'Fleece' and 'fashion firm' pretend to be about clothing; firm is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete as an adjective means solid and definite, as in a firm offer or concrete plan.

clue.text: Maybe telepathy on court saves point

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safely within, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
telepathy is an example of extrasensory perception
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A tennis player reads the opponent's mind on court to save a point.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion lands after the first letter of the joined outer pair, not between them, which is why a quick attempt gives a misspelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A respect is a particular aspect or detail, as in 'in every respect', which is a point.

clue.text: Look with degree of interest around plant

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word goes outside the other

blocks.note: APR, annual percentage rate, measures how much interest is charged
the pea is a plant

explanation.surface: A botanist peers with some curiosity at the vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: To look a certain way is to appear so; both are verbs of seeming.

clue.text: Fish in Italian river with an old, inspiring politician

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the outer letters take the other piece inside

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A fish swimming in an Italian river with an elderly, uplifting statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: The politician is breathed in by the whole string of river, an and old, landing just after the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The pompano is a food fish of warm Atlantic waters.

clue.text: Encourage holy man to abstain from fish

indicators.note: to abstain from something is to do without it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for saint
the surgeon, or surgeonfish, is a tropical reef fish

explanation.surface: A cleric is urged to go without fish, as on a fast day.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone on is to spur them forward, to encourage them.

clue.text: At sea, lose oar in spray

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rower out in the ocean drops a paddle amid the sea spray.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a can that releases its contents as a fine mist.

clue.text: Cold potato fritter to start

indicators.note: to start points at the beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: aloo is the Hindi word for potato, familiar from Indian menus
the opening letter of fritter

explanation.surface: A chilled potato pakora served as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' sounds like serving a starter, but it selects the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and unfriendly, which is a cold manner.

clue.text: Fast time for Mo Farah?

blocks.note: surface reading: a quick race time posted by the Olympic distance runner
setter's reading: the month of fasting observed by Muslims, of whom the athlete is one

explanation.walkthrough: Mo Farah is a British Olympic champion runner and a Muslim, so 'fast time' is both a quick result and a religious month of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic holy month when Muslims fast from dawn until sunset.

clue.text: What a writer needs following drive – booze

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the writer's need is placed behind the road abbreviation

blocks.note: Dr is the street abbreviation for drive
a writer with a pen needs ink

explanation.surface: An author needs a stiff one after the motorway journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is informal for alcoholic drink, and both work as noun or verb.

clue.text: Unusual path with river further east than expected

indicators.text: with river further east than expected
indicators.note: in an across entry east is rightward, so one letter is shifted later in the word than its usual place

blocks.note: a route is a path

explanation.surface: A walking trail along a waterway runs more eastward than planned.
explanation.walkthrough: River is R; in ROUTE it is moved from the front to the fourth slot, nearer the east end.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, borrowed from French, means unconventional or bizarre.

clue.text: Healthcare professional's the first to internalise criticism

indicators.note: to internalise is to take within, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
first abbreviates to 1ST, and 1 is read as I
a rap is a rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: A clinician is the first to take negative feedback to heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist treats patients, so is a kind of medical or psychological professional.

clue.text: Oldest trees men note riddled with disease

blocks.note: firs are conifers
TB, tuberculosis, is a disease
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
N is short for note

explanation.surface: A forest of conifers and its workers are all blighted by illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The disease goes in front of the men and note, as if they were afflicted by it.
explanation.definitionFit: The firstborn child of a family is the eldest.

clue.text: In tune with unmarried primate

indicators.note: un- undoes the married state, telling us to strip out the letter that stands for married

blocks.note: a monkey is a primate

explanation.surface: A tuneful ape that never wed.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the standard abbreviation for married, so MONKEY loses its M.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing on key means singing at the right pitch, in tune.
